grade.rationale: The models are concise and readable, and the derived freshness logic is straightforward. The main weakness is that collection-valued records do not provide stable immutable snapshots or true value-based equality, despite otherwise presenting as immutable value objects.

summary: Well-structured model definitions with one maintainability and correctness concern around collection ownership and record equality. No test coverage conclusions can be drawn from the supplied evidence, and the successful .NET build reported no analyzer findings for this file.

grade.rationale: The state counts and freshness calculation are logically correct, but externally mutable collection instances can change a report or options object after construction.
Collection-backed record properties have shallow, reference-based equality and unclear ownership, which can create surprising behavior in comparisons, caching, and copied options.
Names, defaults, and derived properties communicate their purposes clearly with little incidental complexity.
The dedicated exception type supports contextual failures, although collection invariants are not enforced by these models themselves.
The models are deterministic and easy to instantiate, but mutable collection aliasing can make equality assertions and fixture reuse unexpectedly fragile; coverage remains unknown.

findings.title: Collection-valued records are neither immutable snapshots nor structurally comparable
findings.description: `StalenessReport` and `StalenessEvaluatorOptions` store `IReadOnlyList<T>` references directly. That interface prevents mutation through the declared property but does not prevent callers from retaining and mutating the underlying list or array, so counts and option behavior can change after construction. In addition, generated record equality compares these collections using their own equality implementation, which is normally reference equality; two otherwise identical instances containing independently created lists therefore compare unequal, and `with` copies share the same collection reference.
findings.recommendation: Use an immutable collection type such as `ImmutableArray<T>` and defensively materialize incoming sequences. If these types are not intended to have structural value equality, consider ordinary sealed classes instead of records; otherwise implement explicit sequence-based equality and hashing.
